text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Denmark has a current account deficit for the first time since 1990, with the period March-May showing a 1.3 billion crown shortfall but experts and Danish finance minister Mogens Lykketoft are confident that the situation will improve and there will be a surplus for whole year 1997. Some economists are calling for government action to curb domestic consumption.

--Support for the EU's Amsterdam Treaty reforms within the ruling Social Democratic Party is almost total, while the far-left Socialist Peoples Party remains increasingly split on the issue. Danes are to vote in a referendum on the Amsterdam Treaty reforms next year.
--Danish mink farms are seriously threatened by an epidemic of distemper, with 24 cases of the deadly disease reported to the veterinary authorities. There are 3,000 mink farmers in Denmark.

--The purchase by Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction (PSC) of a 48 percent share in Danish shipbuilding and shipping group J.Lauritzen's Danyard is to go ahead after months of doubt and delay after Lauritzen reached final agreement on the deal in Kuala Lumpur.
